title: Attorney General of Vermont

context.text: Vermont elects its Attorney General to a two-year term. Incumbent Charity Clark is seeking a third term.

H. Brooke Paige, who has entered Republican primaries for statewide offices so that Democratic write-in candidates cannot win those nominations, a practice Vermont Public reports he has followed for a decade, won the Republican primary for Attorney General and then withdrew; the Vermont Republican committee chose Ed Kemon as the replacement.

candidates.name: Charity Clark
candidates.ballotNote: Renominated in the August 11 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Protecting Vermont from federal actions she says violate the Constitution or federal law; her campaign says she has sued the Trump administration 49 times and her office's September 14 release describes its 70th case.
Children's online safety and data privacy, including suits against Meta and TikTok and support for a data privacy bill.
Environmental protection, including a suit against Monsanto over PCB contamination of water resources and schools.
Consumer protection and scam awareness, including a suit against pharmacy benefit managers over prescription drug costs.
Public safety, including prosecuting violent crimes and sexual crimes against children.

statements.quote: Charity took every opportunity to support our right to abortion
statements.context: On her campaign site, which also cites her suit against the FDA over medication abortion access and her defense of a Vermont law on crisis pregnancy centers

record.text: Joined the Federal Trade Commission and 21 other state attorneys general on August 31, 2026 in a lawsuit against Amazon alleging deceptive and unfair practices that inflated prices in its online search advertising auctions.

Joined 21 other states and the District of Columbia on September 14, 2026 in suing to halt the Department of Homeland Security's 2026 public charge rule; her office described it as the 70th case she has brought against the Trump administration since January 2025.

Announced on September 18, 2026 a multistate settlement with Credit Acceptance Corporation, joined by 40 state attorneys general; Vermont's share is $701,251, including restitution to 87 consumers and debt relief to 60 consumers.

Argued in the federal case in which U.S. District Judge Mary Kay Lanthier dismissed, on September 17, 2026, the Department of Justice's lawsuit demanding Vermont's unredacted voter list; the court agreed the statute DOJ relied on does not authorize that demand.

candidates.name: Ed Kemon
candidates.ballotNote: Chosen by the Vermont Republican committee to replace H. Brooke Paige, who won the Republican primary and then withdrew from this race.
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, questionnaire response or public statement from Kemon was found; Vermont Public reported multiple unsuccessful attempts to schedule an interview with him. The slate comes from the Vermont Secretary of State's qualified-candidates file and a Vermont Public report; Vermont's certified-results page was not separately checked.

researchNotes: Slate: Vermont Secretary of State's 2026 general-election qualified-candidates file lists two candidates (Clark, Kemon), consistent with Vermont Public and WCAX reporting after the party's replacement of Paige. Clark's record items come from her office's own press releases. Only Clark's campaign-site statement on abortion is recorded as a position-related statement; she did not take a documented side on other listed issues in the material reviewed.
